findings.title: Fallback lookup crashes when site default locale is nil
findings.body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb line 17 FallbackLocaleList#[] builds [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. Calling to_sym before compact means a nil site setting raises NoMethodError instead of being removed by compact. Any translation that needs fallback resolution then raises instead of falling back to English, turning a missing string into a 500 error. This is reachable during boot, migrations, tests, or if Redis/DB is unavailable. Fix by handling nil/blank safely before to_sym.

findings.title: Translation cache ignores fallback chain and poisons misses
findings.body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 72 the cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}" with no site default locale or fallback list. A key missing in the user locale but present in the fallback locale caches the fallback result under only the user locale. Changing SiteSetting.default_locale later still returns the old cached language, and worse a lookup done before fallback files are loaded caches the 'translation missing' string forever until eviction or I18n.reload!. Fix by including the resolved fallback chain in the key and not caching missing translations, and invalidating on locale-setting change.

findings.title: Translate preloads only current locale, ignores fallbacks and explicit locale
findings.body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 67 I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale) and never loads the fallback locales (site default, :en). It also ignores an explicit locale option in args when deciding what to load. So I18n.t(key, locale: :de) while global locale is :en only ensures :en is loaded, and any use outside ApplicationController#set_locale (Sidekiq, mailers, console, explicit-locale emails) gets 'translation missing' even though the string exists in the fallback file, because on-demand loading never loaded that file. Fix by ensuring the full fallback chain for the requested locale inside translate.

findings.title: DB lookup on every fallback resolution
findings.body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback resolution, i.e. on every translation miss. That puts a SiteSetting (Redis/DB-backed) lookup on the hot translation path, adding overhead per missing key plus per-request ensure_loaded! cost, and makes all translated error pages depend on DB availability. If the DB is down during early boot or outage, translation itself raises. Memoize/cache the site locale per request or fall back to I18n.default_locale without DB access.

findings.title: No tests for fallback order and lazy loading
findings.body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb a new user-locale to site-locale to English fallback chain plus on-demand loading is introduced, but the pull request changes no specs. There is no coverage that a missing key in the user locale resolves from the site locale then English, that fallback files are loaded on demand in controllers and background jobs, or that explicit locale arguments work. Regressions in ordering or missing-file handling would ship undetected.
